source.title: Your LLM, Your Style: Behavioral Mode Axes for LLM Behavioral Control
source.authors: Haoze Liu; Run-Ke Liu; Hai-Ying Xu; Jia-Hui Han; Si-Yuan Fang; Si-Yu Yan; Huiqi Deng; Guan-Chun Wang; Na Zou

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests the narrow V4 possibility of SAE-recoverable features in LLMs by training a sparse autoencoder and interpreting features aligned with behavioral axes. It does not test superposition or feature-capacity competition.
record.gate_note: The paper reports SAE features associated with thought- and response-derived BMAs, recorded below for V4. Its behavioral steering results and the cosine geometry of the BMA directions are not rows: they do not measure superposition or the dimensionality of underlying model features. The paper also cites activation-steering work, but cited findings are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The SAE is used only as a diagnostic readout tool (Appendix H: 'diagnostic only'). The paper projects dense behavioral axes onto it and interprets two features. It reports no reconstruction quality, sparsity-versus-fidelity numbers, recoverability rate or comparison to a baseline. It also makes no claim about whether LLMs contain SAE-recoverable sparse features or spread features across neurons. The two feature descriptions are an application of a dictionary, not a test of V4. No other version (superposition geometry, capacity, polysemanticity, canonical units, dimensionality) is measured.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct, but incomplete. The authors conclude three things. Situated behavioral profiles differ substantially from questionnaire self-reports (mean gap 22.7 points) and are stable within a register but shift across registers. Behavioral modes are causally controllable via BMAs, whose clean effects concentrate in model-specific Behavioral Control Layer bands. Thought-derived BMAs give cleaner control than response-derived BMAs, which are prone to trait drift. The SAE is explicitly diagnostic, and no claims about superposition are made.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses activation-space behavioral axes and SAE feature inspection, not the toy-network setup or superposition measurements of the original source.
record.method_sensitivity: Behavioral steering effects vary by layer; the paper reports clean control concentrated in model-specific earlier-to-middle BCL bands. This layer sensitivity concerns the study's BMA control results, not superposition.

fits_no_version.finding: In Llama-3.1-8B layer 8, the 20 thought-derived behavioral axes are largely near-orthogonal: median |cos| 0.13, 85% of pairs below 0.3, eight above 0.5. Thought- and response-derived axes have mean cosine 0.37. Near-orthogonal foreign axes still move target choices by a mean of 36 points, against a norm-matched random-direction floor of 9.1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Linear steering directions for distinct behavioral modes occupy largely separate directions, yet transfer non-specifically to other behaviors' choices. This concerns steering-vector geometry and specificity, not superposition.

record.problems: The SAE feature evidence is diagnostic and qualitative, and the reported feature examples concern one behavioral pattern in Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. It does not establish feature completeness, stability, or general recoverability, nor does it measure superposition.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant rows. BMA steering outcomes and pairwise BMA cosine results are omitted because they do not measure superposition or underlying feature dimensionality.

untested.parts: All of it: no toy models, no sparsity transition, no feature geometry.
All of it: no neuron-level capacity analysis.
All of it: no polysemantic-neuron analysis.
Whether features spread across neurons, and whether an SAE recovers sparse features. The SAE is only used; no quality or recoverability metrics are reported.
Completeness, stability or canonicity of SAE features. Only one SAE size, with no cross-seed or cross-size comparison.
Whether the superposed features are one-dimensional. The BMAs are single directions by construction.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's relation 'tests'/T3 and its V4 'supports' label are not justified. Interpreting two hand-picked SAE latents is a use of dictionary learning, not evidence about it. SAE details for reference: BatchTopK, 131,072 latents, k=64, 500M tokens, Llama-3.1-8B layer 8 (also analyzing layers 7 and 11) and Qwen2.5-7B layer 11. No fidelity metrics are reported. Steering uses dense axes throughout.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model superposition, feature overlap, and sparsity-dependent transitions and geometry.
Whether polysemantic neurons result from competition for limited representational capacity.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise without capacity pressure.
Does not test feature spread across neurons or broad SAE feature recoverability; the SAE analysis is limited to features associated with behavioral axes.
Does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Does not test whether the underlying represented features are one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Trained a sparse autoencoder at the BCL and projected the thought-derived BMA onto its features.
rows.measure: SAE feature interpretation and alignment with the BMA
rows.value: Feature 17024 is interpreted as improvisation and adapting on the fly, and its alignment with BMA-T is marked on-construct.
rows.note: The SAE analysis is described as diagnostic; steering uses dense axes, not SAE features.
rows.check: This is a qualitative interpretation of one SAE latent (17024) that a BMA-T direction projects onto. It uses the SAE as a tool. It has no baseline, no recoverability or fidelity measure, and no reported projection magnitude, so it cannot show whether V4 holds.

rows.value: Feature 103914 is interpreted as indifference or a low-effort rationale, and its alignment with BMA-R is marked off-construct as trait drift.
rows.note: The authors use this feature as a diagnostic of response-axis drift, not as evidence that SAE features are canonical or complete units.
rows.check: This is a qualitative interpretation of one SAE latent (103914) used to diagnose drift along the response-derived axis. It uses the SAE as a tool with no measure of feature recoverability. 'Off-construct' describes the BMA-R direction, not the SAE.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: The reported SAE analysis of improvisation-related BMAs in Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
reader_labels.reason: The SAE analysis identifies interpretable sparse features aligned with the thought- and response-derived axes (R1–R2); this is narrow evidence of SAE-recoverable features, not evidence about feature spread across neurons.
